newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank, Germany's central bank, said it left all its key interest rates unchanged at its council meeting on Wednesday.

The discount rate remains at 2.50 percent, the Lombard rate at 4.50 percent. The Bundesbank also said it would set the next two weekly tenders for securities repurchase agreements, or repos, at a fixed rate of 3 percent.
The repo rate has been fixed at 3 percent since last August.
Economists had not expected any change on interest rates as they argued inflation was still under control, eliminating the need to tighten credit at this time.
Economists also said the central bank's monetary policy was already quite expansive and that there was little else the central bank could do to stimulate economic growth.
The central bank last cut its discount and Lombard rates in April 1996.
The Bundesbank's regular biweekly policy-making council meeting was held one day earlier than usual this week because Thursday, May Day, is a public holiday.
